analysis.title: The Spectrum of Energy - US Midterms, Europe & Asia LNG, and Global Distillates
key_insights: Piper's policy team gives 55% odds to a Democratic sweep of the midterms, 30% to a divided Congress and 15% to a GOP sweep. The midterms matter little for the Mideast and Russia wars but a lot for US energy permitting reform.

The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) would cap federal environmental decisions at 2 years, narrow NEPA, strengthen FERC backstop authority for transmission and push data centers to supply more power behind the meter. Piper's policy team puts 50/50 odds on it becoming law this year, versus about 40% in betting markets.

Lame-duck risks to BAAJA include Trump administration interference with offshore wind permitting, House Republicans feeling little ownership, Democrats renegotiating if they outperform, and limited floor time. Government funding (Dec 11 deadline) and an Iran war supplemental rank ahead of it.

Europe is in a more precarious LNG position than Asia this winter. Qatar's roughly 20% of global LNG supply is offline, European storage is in deficit, and there is no new US supply for about one more year. Weather decides which bloc pays up.

The EU Commission confirmed a full ban on Russian LNG imports from January 1, 2027, including legacy long-term contracts. That removes more than 2 bcf/d of imports. Russia would also have to ship Arctic cargoes much farther, 20 to 37 days to Asia versus 7 days to Europe.
TTF quoted EUR100/MWh as early late-October cold cut European storage fill rates. JKM trades at a premium to TTF for Q1-27.

Globally traded middle distillates (diesel and jet) are down 1.3 mb/d (about 14%) in 2026. Mideast supply fell about 700 kb/d out of an 8.5 mb/d global trade after Iranian retaliation. Russian exports fell about 600 kb/d from May/June because of Ukrainian refinery strikes.

Piper's base case, if the wars continue, is distillate inventories grinding lower, with Europe the one to watch. Even if Russia and China add supply, global balances would not normalize, and restoring Mideast exports needs the wars to settle.

Mideast refinery runs are about 15% below 2025 and 10% below the 4-year average. Mideast net diesel exports are 55% below February's 1.4 mb/d high and 38% below last year. Russian refinery runs are just under 4 mb/d, with utilization near 60% versus about 70% in Q1.

Piper cuts its oil forecast framing to a new normal and takes the over on consensus. It expects Brent in a $70-90/b range averaging $80/b through H2 and 2027, with WTI about $5/b lower. It sees upside risk given residual all-out war odds and about 9 mb/d of crude that exits only via the Strait of Hormuz.

US natural gas is called bearish short term. Henry Hub is below $3/MMBtu and Q3 averaged $2.94/MMBtu versus Piper's $2.75 forecast. Piper keeps a long-term target of $3.50/MMBtu (about the Haynesville breakeven). Supply growth is strong, LNG utilization disappoints, and El Nino skews winter weather mild.
US weekly data was constructive. Commercial crude drew 8.5 mb for a fourth straight week, and crude plus key product stocks drew another 5 mb to a new 2026 low. The US rig count is unchanged at 603.
Piper models NEVs displacing about 970 kb/d of road fuel demand now, rising to 2.3 mb/d by 2030. It sees global light-duty vehicle fuel demand peaking near 31.4 mb/d in 2029.

Global NEV sales were about 1.9m units in August, up 1% y/y, with a record 29% share of new car sales. China's NEV share passed 60%. US NEV sales are down 31% y/y year to date and the US share is 7.1%.

The EPA's final RFS volumes for 2026-27 raise total renewable fuel to about 26 billion gallons, up 16% from 2025. Piper calls this bullish for biofuel margins and RIN prices, with RD/BD utilization needing about 88% in 2026 and over 90% in 2027.
The NRC approved TVA's 300 MW BWRX-300 SMR at Clinch River in 14 months, faster than the 18 months in EO 14300. It is the second commercial SMR approval this year after TerraPower in March.
Piper's equity coverage: John Royall rates DINO overweight and PARR, DK and PBF neutral. He initiated COP and OXY at neutral. Dimple Gosai initiated GNRC at overweight on data center backup power.

Piper's energy portfolio is up 26.6% year to date and 7.3% since the war began. Integrated oils and refiners are up 56.8% YTD and 35.6% since the war began, while NEVs are down 20.7% since the war began.

risk_factors: Colder than normal winter in NW Europe, NE Asia or the northeast US with low European storage and Qatar offline.
Escalation of the Mideast war, including attacks on Saudi Arabia, would hit about 9 mb/d of crude, 10+ bcf/d of LNG and 3 mb/d of products tied to the Strait of Hormuz.
Further Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries could cut diesel exports further.
BAAJA could slip to the next Congress if lame-duck time runs out or Democrats seek better terms.
Cost indices for E&Ps and oilfield services are rising faster than average per the Dallas Fed survey.
charts_described: Table of energy sub-sector performance shows Integrated Oils + Refiners up 56.8% YTD and 35.6% since the war began, NEVs down 20.7% since the war began, and the total energy portfolio up 26.6% YTD.
Brent price forecast table shows Piper Brent at $97 in Q2-26, $91 in Q3-26 and $89 for 2026, against a consensus of $95 for 2026 and a strip of $99.
Senate race table lists NC (Cooper, +10.6 Dem margin, Likely Dem), OH (Brown, +3.3, Lean Dem), TX (Toss Up, +1.5) and ME (Toss Up, +1.4) among Republican-held seats in play.
vol_and_positioning: Piper says the only bullish factor in US natural gas in Q4 so far is extremely bearish positioning.
Brent is expected to trade a $70-90/b range with volatility. Piper's 4 Hormuz scenarios include two with 70% odds in which Tehran controls traffic.
geopolitical: Iran retaliation against US-Israeli attacks halved Mideast diesel and jet exports. Iran says it will not open the Strait of Hormuz until the US lifts its blockade and releases funds.
Iran requires the Lebanon, Gaza and Houthi-Saudi wars to settle before real talks, and its security chief said no enriched uranium will leave Iranian territory.
Egypt's president asked parliament to vote on 10/26 on sending troops to Saudi Arabia. The UK is putting a Typhoon squadron over Saudi Arabia. The Pentagon is reportedly readying more troops.
Ukraine's strikes on Russian refineries cut Russian refinery utilization to about 60%. Russia partially lifted its diesel export ban earlier this month.
The EU will fully ban Russian LNG imports from January 1, 2027.
Piper's policy team expects an Iran war supplemental in the lame-duck session, and US midterms on the November ballot.

tension_points.bull_case: Piper sees Brent averaging $80/b through H2 2026 and 2027 because about 9 mb/d of Mideast crude, 10+ bcf/d of LNG and 3 mb/d of products depend on Hormuz, with upside risk from all-out war.
tension_points.bear_case: Consensus bearish narratives treat the June 17 MoU as the end of the conflict, and the market repeatedly sells off on diplomacy headlines.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A durable Mideast settlement that reopens the Strait of Hormuz.

tension_points.bull_case: Cold or normal weather with low storage, Qatar offline and Russian LNG banned from January 1 would send TTF sharply higher.
tension_points.bear_case: A strong El Nino could deliver a warm winter, freeing Asian cargoes for Europe and extending the injection season.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A warm winter in NW Europe and NE Asia.

tension_points.bull_case: Cold winter weather could draw storage down and surprise demand, with LNG exports growing.
tension_points.bear_case: Relentless supply growth, a storage surplus, mild El Nino weather and weak LNG utilization keep prices under $3/MMBtu.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A cold November that surprises demand despite ample supply.

theme_stances.key_argument: Europe lacks the storage to get through a severe winter and a Russian LNG ban removes more than 2 bcf/d of imports.
theme_stances.evidence: Europe is in the more precarious position.

theme_stances.key_argument: Ample supply growth and mild El Nino weather keep US gas prices bearish.
theme_stances.evidence: Ample supply and plenty ways to grow it
